subject: Post-call: p95/p99 tail envelope, concurrency & streaming follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@pinecrest.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: p95/p99 tail envelope, concurrency & streaming follow-up

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the performance qualification:  

Summary of what we heard from your side on the call:
- Primary objective: confirm end-to-end p95/p99 for the live inference path (client -> API -> model -> response) under production-like traffic.
- Current provider numbers (your input): p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 1.2s for the 800-token median workload you run; peaks during batch jobs push p99 closer to 2s.
- Streaming usage: roughly 35% of requests use streaming (server-sent token chunks). Typical concurrency for streaming sessions is 80–120 concurrent streams during morning peak.
- Throughput baseline: 1.2k requests/min average in production with 4x spikes during scheduled batch ingestion.

What we propose as the qualification plan (high level):
1) Traffic envelope: reproduce your 1.2k/min baseline + 4x spike with the same token distribution you shared (median 800 tokens, 95th 1.6k tokens). We asked you to attach a small sample traffic CSV — thanks in advance.
2) p95/p99 objective bands: validate Redwood hosted API under two policies:
   - Latency-prioritized path (reserved compute, smaller batching) — target p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms for non-streaming requests;
   - Cost-balanced path (auto-batching, KV prefix caching) — expected p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 1.2s.
   For streaming sessions, we’ll validate token-by-token latency (first-byte and tail) and end-to-end completion latencies; targets will be detailed in the PoC matrix below.
3) Concurrency matrix: run tests at 50, 80, 120, 200 concurrent streaming sessions; for non-streaming concurrency test at 200, 500, and 1000 concurrent requests.
4) Acceptance criteria: pass if p95/p99 are within +/-20% of the target bands above across 3 run windows and no functional errors.

Action items from our side (Camila/SDR + Eng):
- Camila: schedule two engineering session windows (POC kickoff + deep run) with your ops team.
- Karthik: own the POC configuration and the test harness (load generator + trace capture).
- Jasmine: prepare Redwood-hosted config variants (latency-prioritized vs cost-balanced) and baseline scripts for KV/prefix caching.

Requested items from Pinecrest (please attach if possible):
- Sample traffic envelope CSV (timestamps, token counts, streaming flag) — small anonymized sample is fine.
- Representative p95/p99 traces or HAR-style logs from your current provider for a 24-hour window.
- Any custom decoding/streaming timeouts you enforce on the client side.

I attached a short POC matrix (redwood-poc-matrix.xlsx) and a template for traces/traffic. Proposed dates: kickoff 2026-10-25 for a 60–90 minute sync, deep run 2026-11-02 for the stress runs.

If that sounds good, please share the CSV and traces and we’ll lock the kickoff.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Engaged Solutions, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood-poc-matrix.xlsx (workbook), traffic-envelope-sample.csv (sample)
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@pinecrest.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Li <evan@pinecrest.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 tail envelope, concurrency & streaming follow-up

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear plan. Attached a small sample (pinecrest-current-p95p99-traces.csv) — note that we redacted user ids. A couple clarifications and current-state numbers from our infra team:  

- Confirming current provider median: ~820 tokens, p95: 210ms, p99: 1.2s. During scheduled batch ingestion (daily ETL) we see tail spikes: p99 can reach 1.9–2.1s for non-streaming requests.
- Streaming specifics: our streaming sessions are implemented client-side with a 4s chunking window; first-byte latency is usually ~120ms but completion (final token) can introduce jitter because of our buffering.
- Concurrency we see today: sustained 85 concurrent streams in regular traffic, peaks to 160 during daytime bursts.

Two notes on acceptance: 1) we must not regress on first-byte for streaming (first-byte target <= 200ms), and 2) any solution that trades away determinism on tail (p99) under the ETL spike profile is disqualifying without an explicit fallback routing policy.

We can confirm kickoff on 2026-10-25 at 10:00am PT; Evan (cc) will share a runbook and access to a small test cluster for load generation.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Pinecrest Analytics
sarah@pinecrest.io | +1 (617) 555-0912

Attachment: pinecrest-current-p95p99-traces.csv
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@pinecrest.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 tail envelope, concurrency & streaming follow-up

Perfect — appreciate the sample and the clarity on first-byte constraints. Quick notes before the kickoff: 

- Karthik/Jasmine: please review Sarah’s two hard constraints (first-byte <= 200ms for streaming; no p99 regressions under ETL spike) and prepare the config variants. Jasmine, can you include a TTL/kv-prefix-cache enabled variant + a small-quantization variant? We want to understand tradeoffs.
- Sarah/Evan: can you confirm if the ETL spike is a scheduled cron job we can reproduce in your test cluster or if it’s an emergent workload? Also confirm the client chunking window (Sarah noted 4s) — we’ll simulate identical behavior in our generator.

I’ll lock the 10:00am PT kickoff and send a calendar invite with a short agenda (discuss runbook, confirm sample ingestion, quick demo of Redwood-hosted variants).

Thanks — Camila
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Pre-kickoff checklist and ownership (Pinecrest PoC)

Internal checklist (owners & notes) ahead of 10/25 kickoff: 

- Karthik (owner) — Test harness: finalize Gatling script + custom streaming generator; include toggles for chunk_window_ms and client_buffering. Deliverable: git branch redwood/pinecrest-load by 2026-10-22 EOD.
- Jasmine (owner) — Redwood-hosted configs: produce three variants in the PoC workbook: 
   A) latency-prioritized (smaller batch size, reserved capacity)
   B) cost-balanced (aggressive batching + prefix caching)
   C) fallback-routing enabled (auto-fallback to smaller model instance under tail pressure)
  Deliverable: redwood-poc-matrix.xlsx updated with run commands and expected tokenization profile by 2026-10-23.
- Camila (owner) — PoC coordination, calendar invite, acceptance criteria email and HubSpot update (set deal stage to POC Scheduled).

Measurement plan (quick):
- Capture first-byte and inter-token latencies for streaming; compute per-run p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and total completion.
- For non-streaming: export percentiles, and collect flame/traces for any >1s tail event.

Contingency: if p99 exceeds target by >30% on two consecutive runs, enable fallback-routing option C and re-run.

Notes: include the attachments Sarah provided in the PoC drive folder and flag any anomalies before the kickoff.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Engaged Solutions, Redwood Inference
